name: CA-31
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's 8-point Democratic lean plus a favorable national environment
Cisneros's large fundraising advantage over Ching
No public polling of the general election
model.rationale: The fundamentals point to a comfortable incumbent win: an 8-point Democratic district, a Democratic-leaning environment, and Cisneros out-raising Ching roughly nine to one, with markets pricing him around 96%. With no polling to contradict that picture, the forecast stays near the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Ching competitive, or a surge of Republican outside spending, would warrant revisiting the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Gil Cisneros, the Democratic incumbent, advanced to the general election against Republican Eric Ching in a district that leans Democratic by about eight points. Cisneros holds a decisive financial edge, raising roughly $705,000 to Ching's $82,000, and has modest outside support with no recorded opposition spending. No public polls of the race are available, and no expert raters have published ratings, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, money, and the broader political environment, all of which favor the incumbent.

Prediction markets price Cisneros around 96 percent, consistent with a comfortable expected margin near 20 points. The main uncertainty is the absence of direct polling, which keeps uncertainty somewhat elevated despite the lopsided fundamentals.
